caption: The drawing features a single object resembling a decorative metal piece, positioned centrally on a plain, off-white background. The object is predominantly brown with subtle greenish and bronze hues, giving it a metallic appearance. The top section displays two long, upward-curving extensions with rounded ends, similar to antennae or stylized horns. Below these are symmetrical, rounded protrusions on either side resembling eyes, and a central, bulbous form. Along the length of the object’s elongated body, there is a symmetrical arrangement of three pairs of small, rounded, paw-like shapes, which are evenly spaced. The central body is adorned with textured, raised, rounded bumps within a bordered area that runs vertically down its length. At the tapered lower end of the object is a small circular hole. The artist’s signature, "M McAuley," is present in the lower right corner.
title: Bootjack
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
